sentence: This project offers experimental tools and computer analysis to help researchers study single cells, including their RNA and surface proteins.
This project provides organ models made from patient cells, including organ-on-a-chip systems, so researchers can study diseases related to cystic fibrosis.
This project tries to find out how genetic variants linked to the centromere cause chromosomal errors and early pregnancy loss.
This project studies how the structure of DNA in cells helps cells respond to stress and what happens when this control is lost.
This project supplies patient tumor and normal tissues and provides tissue analysis services for research on brain tumors.
This project combines a microscopy technique with computer processing to image how cells move in living organisms.
This project studies the sensory nerves that reach the cornea, looking at their form, molecules and function in mouse models.
This project studies how T cells change the behavior of skin cells after inflammation, using cell cultures, mice and patient samples.
This project builds a machine learning tool and a conversational agent to predict the risk of major adverse cardiac events in people with chest pain.
This project uses capillary electrophoresis and mass spectrometry to find protein forms that guide early cell development in zebrafish embryos.
This project uses computer simulations to study how pulling, pushing, stretching and squeezing forces change the behavior of proteins.
This project studies how faulty versions of a sodium channel gene cause seizures and tries to develop viral and CRISPR treatments in mice.
This project studies how mitochondria affect monocyte development after chemotherapy and whether this helps tumors spread.
This project builds a way to find out which molecules plants can make by switching on many biochemical programs at once.
This project builds computer tools that predict how mutations interact and how their combined effects add up.
This project builds mass spectrometry methods to measure the proteins in different cell populations inside organoids.
This project finishes work to find the genetic cause of Mendelian conditions, using data from participant samples.
This project develops chemical probes and mass spectrometry footprinting to study how a human glucose transport protein interacts with anticancer drug candidates and partner proteins.
This project studies how a gene that causes a congenital disorder of glycosylation controls growth and developmental signaling.
This project develops NanoDiscs as a vaccine platform for treating celiac disease.
